items.title: AI与倍数：AI如何重写私募股权价值创造Playbook
items.snippet: AI技术正在重塑PE行业价值创造策略，通过提升运营效率重构企业估值Multiple模型，改变传统Buyout逻辑。
items.raw_snippet: # AI and the Multiple: How AI Is Rewriting the Private Equity Value-Creation Playbook. Here is how artificial intelligence now moves the number that decides an exit, and why the window to build it is open right now. * Buyers are repricing in real time. Deal advisors are telling owners that multiples are softening for software and services businesses that are not generating AI intellectual property. * AI moves enterprise value through three levers: it drives cost out, it shifts a business into the tech-enabled category, and it builds proprietary IP the company owns at exit. * The third lever is the one most firms miss, and it is where the durable premium sits. Investment bankers and deal advisors are telling founders and CEOs a version of the same thing: the multiple is softening for any software or services business that is not generating artificial intelligence as part of what it does.

items.title: AI融资：真正的转折点 - Bertrand Duperrin
items.snippet: 探讨AI Funding是否进入理性回归阶段，从疯狂炒作转向实际应用价值评估的关键Turning Point，预示市场成熟度提升。
items.raw_snippet: We know we have a technology in our hands that can—and indeed will—revolutionize the world; that is no longer in question. Because the question on everyone’s mind isn’t whether AI can create value for its stakeholders and users, but whether **it can create enough value so that everyone benefits financially**, whether, ultimately, it will justify the hundreds of billions invested in this technological race, and, above all, when. At first glance, these are topics that mainly interest investors, but I wonder if they aren’t telling us something much more fundamental about the sector and an ecosystem that is gradually reaching a point where **the question is no longer just how much to invest, but who is still willing to do so**, under what conditions, and for how long. * *The debate is shifting: it no longer focuses primarily on AI’s performance or potential, but rather on the cost of capital, the time required to reach profitability, and investors’ willingness to continue funding this transition phase.*.

items.raw_snippet: For debt collection agencies, debt buyers, creditors, collection law firms, and fintech leaders, this shift matters because AI adoption is beginning to influence how organizations are evaluated by clients, investors, buyers, and strategic partners. In that sense, AI-driven industry bifurcation and M&A are becoming closely connected. It is about which organizations can convert technology into measurable operational improvements, stronger margins, better governance and compliance, and more scalable business models. In that case, the next competitive advantage in financial services will belong to organizations that understand AI as a strategic capability rather than a narrow software deployment. AI-driven industry bifurcation and M&A describe a growing divide between companies that are actively using AI to improve business performance and those that are still evaluating whether to act. A business with strong revenue but limited technology infrastructure may not be viewed the same way as a company with comparable revenue, scalable workflows, clean data architecture, and a clear AI deployment roadmap.

items.title: OpenAI Proposes 5% Federal Government Stake to Defuse ...
items.snippet: # OpenAI Proposes 5% Federal Government Stake to Defuse Regulatory Pressure: Rep...
items.raw_snippet: # OpenAI Proposes 5% Federal Government Stake to Defuse Regulatory Pressure: Reports. In a bold bid to defuse intensifying regulatory scrutiny and address public anxiety over the economic disruptions of artificial intelligence (AI), OpenAI has proposed granting the U.S. government a 5% equity stake in the company, according to reports published Thursday. The proposal envisions a broader arrangement under which all leading American AI developers — including Anthropic, Google, and Meta Platforms Inc. — would cede a similar 5% stake to the government. OpenAI’s pitch aims to create a “public wealth fund” that distributes the economic benefits of AI directly to citizens, particularly targeting Americans who lack traditional market investments. While Trump has previously called a government ownership stake in tech giants “a beautiful thing” that would make Americans “partners in this revolution,” the proposal may face a steep uphill battle. Furthermore, some lawmakers argue a 5% stake is insufficient; Sen. Sanders has advocated for a more sweeping 50% public stake to compensate for the industry’s unauthorized use of human data.

items.snippet: * AI search tools increasingly rely on Wikipedia when recommending lawyers, maki...
items.raw_snippet: * AI search tools increasingly rely on Wikipedia when recommending lawyers, making Wikipedia visibility a growing factor in legal marketing and client acquisition. * Lawyers and law firms seeking Wikipedia pages must satisfy strict neutrality, verifiability, and notability standards, not merely demonstrate career success. A few issues ago, I wrote about how potential law firm clients were beginning to rely on AI to find lawyers and why that might reshape SEO and Google’s dominance in lawyer search. In looking at ChatGPT, they found Wikipedia to be the top source, cited 35.6% of the time—meaning large law firms, which dominate Wikipedia, benefit disproportionately. Wikipedia notes that articles can be “mercilessly edited,” so once an article about you is on the site, you should be aware that you don’t control what is said. An article about a lawyer or law firm can meet all of the principles of neutrality and verifiability and still be rejected because Wikipedia’s editors may determine that a topic doesn’t warrant an article of its own.

items.title: Yann LeCun致力于开发更灵活的AI系统
items.snippet: Meta首席AI科学家指出当前AI"并不聪明"，正研发具备更高Flexibility和推理能力的新一代AI架构，突破现有LLM局限性。
items.raw_snippet: # AI is 'not smart' so what's next in artificial intelligence? "We don't have robots that are nearly as good at understanding the physical world as a rat," says Yann LeCun, one of the leading figures in the world of artificial intelligence. He worked at Facebook-owner, Meta, for a decade, where he was chief AI scientist, but left in 2025 and founded Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs (AMI Labs). They have their uses, he says, but will never be able to tackle complicated situations in the real world, like getting a robot to do household chores. "They're not a path towards human level or human-like intelligence, or even animal-like intelligence, because they cannot deal with real world data, they just are not built for that," he tells me on the sidelines of VivaTech, France's leading technology conference. So, Paris-based AMI Labs is busy developing a new type of artificial intelligence not based on the tech behind ChatGPT and its rivals.

items.title: Generative AI and Privilege: Why Confidentiality and Counsel Direction Matters
items.snippet: Photo of Generative AI and Privilege: Why Confidentiality and Counsel Direction ...
items.raw_snippet: Photo of Generative AI and Privilege: Why Confidentiality and Counsel Direction Matters. # Generative AI and Privilege: Why Confidentiality and Counsel Direction Matters. The key lesson: privilege and work-product protections are available for AI-assisted work, but only if counsel controls the process from the start. The court held that a defendant’s communications with the public AI platform Claude were not protected by attorney-client privilege. The reasoning was straightforward: Claude is not an attorney, and the defendant was not seeking legal advice from counsel through the tool. The court rejected work-product protection as well, because the materials were not prepared by or at counsel’s direction and did not reflect counsel’s legal strategy at the time of creation. Notably, the *Heppner* court suggested the result might differ if counsel directed the AI use in a way analogous to a non-lawyer professional retained to help an attorney provide legal advice to a client such as circumstances where the professional’s involvement is necessary or highly useful to the lawyer’s legal advice.

items.raw_snippet: # AI in Systems Engineering: A Practical Guide for Complex Product Teams. This guide explains what AI in systems engineering actually is, why most pilots fail, what it can do today, and what it takes to move from a demo to production. ## What is AI in systems engineering? AI in systems engineering applies machine learning and language models to the core work of building complex products: understanding requirements, tracing functions across software and hardware, analyzing the impact of a change, and answering cross-domain questions. Most engineering AI pilots stall for the same reason: they are built on top of fragmented, ungoverned data, so they cannot produce answers an engineer would stake a decision on. Scaling past the pilot is an architecture problem, not a model problem, which is exactly the argument of our paper on scaling industrial AI from pilots to value. The SPREAD platform is built to take engineering AI from pilot to production on one governed source of truth, and you can see the connected model behind it in Product Explorer.
